reasoning: Long oo; taa marbuta after ك is e. The same word also means a thorn.
Long oo, not the MSA diphthong mawt. The verb is maat.
Taa marbuta after ب is e. With the article, in-nakbe is specifically 1948; without it, any disaster.
ض is emphatic D and the first short vowel drops, as in kbiir. Also the everyday word for thin or skinny.
Plural imperative of ittaSal, with emphatic ص. ع plus the article contracts and assimilates to the sun letter ش, giving 3ash-shurTa; taa marbuta after ط is a.
Taa marbuta after ن is e. A clothes cupboard or wardrobe; a kitchen cupboard is usually a khazaane too, or a jaroor for a drawer.

il-7amdu lillah runs together as il-7amdilla in speech, so the Arabic is respelt. 3a plus the article assimilates to the sun letter س. Said to someone back from a trip or out of hospital; the reply is allah ysallmak.
Plain CaCaC past; the broom is a miknase. Used for sweeping a floor with a broom.
Long oo. Collective; a single banana is mooze.
The presentative hayy, as in hayy il-miftaa7, with the shadda doubling the y; the masculine counterpart is hayy or haada. The same spelling also writes hiyye 'she', which the English rules out here.
ق is a glottal stop in everyday use, il-waa'i3. Also the participle 'fallen', but the noun sense is the usual one.
The CaCCaan state adjective, feminine na3saane. Means sleepy, not asleep.
Initial cluster, as in kbiir. Covers a brother-in-law or a son-in-law; the plural nsaayib is the in-law family.
Singulative of the collective ghanam, which is the flock; taa marbuta after م is e. na3je is the more specific word for a ewe.
One syllable, plural klaab. A strong insult when used of a person.
ط is emphatic T and the shadda doubles the y. Of a person it is kind-hearted; the same word is also the discourse marker 'okay' and, of food, tasty.
The short vowel of the first syllable drops in the dialect. The taa marbuta comes out a after ح here; the verb is siba7.
ض is emphatic D. The word is negative in Palestinian: someone who pokes into other people's business. Harmless curiosity would be 3indo fuDuul or just 7abb yi3raf.
snaan is the plural of sinn with the first vowel dropped; plurals take feminine singular agreement, hence bitwajji3ni. Form II, literally they cause me pain.
ط is emphatic T; the word-initial hamza sits on a vowel seat so only the vowel is written. Alif maqsura is romanized a.
س is a sun letter, so is-saa3a; taa marbuta after ع is a. The frame takes the hour between is-saa3a and w 3ashara, as in is-saa3a khamse w 3ashara.

meaning_fix: a gunshot / a round of gunfire
reasoning: ط is emphatic T and ق is a glottal stop; taa marbuta after ق is a. It names a single shot, not the event of a shooting, which would be iTlaa' naar.
ق in wa't is a glottal stop and و is a moon letter. The wording reads like a calque from English; to ask the time a Ramallah speaker says 'addeesh is-saa3a or is-saa3a kam.
been takes the extended base beenaat- before pronoun suffixes, as in beenaatna. The -hum suffix is the Palestinian third plural.
Both ق are glottal stops, and the la- prefix is written as part of its token. been fatra w fatra is an equally common way to say it.
